viewport: all (1440/1920/768/844l/1280s desktop nav; 375/390 Logo, EN/FR, Menu)
description: [KNOWN ISSUE, cause confirmed, FIX VERIFIED in commit 2012874] Keyboard focus landed on header links while the header was translated off-screen (inView false, y -55/-60 in the pass-1 keyboard audit, WCAG 2.4.7 / 2.4.11). Cause: the hide-on-scroll-down ScrollTrigger in Nav.tsx called show(false) -> gsap yPercent:-110 (Nav.tsx:35) without regard to focus. The header stays visible and in the tab order, so Tab-wrap (Skip link -> Logo -> About...) and Shift+Tab from the content put focus on links above the viewport. Re-test on the current tree: forward wrap at 1440 motion gives Skip/Gregory Sutjian/About/Projects/Experience all inView=true, covered=false. At 390: Logo/EN-FR/MENU inView=true. Shift+Tab from the footer at 1440 motion/reduced and at 390: no focused element is off-screen or under the header.
file_line: components/Nav.tsx:35 (cause); fix at Nav.tsx:44 and Nav.tsx:51-52
suggested_fix: Keep the committed fix: focusin on the header calls show(true), and onUpdate skips hiding while header contains :focus-visible. Optional hardening: also call show(true) on keydown Tab when document.activeElement is in the header, and add html{scroll-padding-top:5rem} so content that receives focus is never scrolled under the fixed header.

description: In-page nav links (desktop nav, mobile menu items, logo) scroll the page but never move keyboard focus to the target, so the next Tab continues from the header, and in reduced motion it sends the user back to the hero. 1440 reduced: Enter on 'Projects' scrolls to y=6640 with focus still on the header link. Tab x3 goes EXPERIENCE -> CONTACT -> EN/FR, and the 4th Tab lands on 'View projects' at scrollY 1198, back in the hero. 1440 motion: focus stays on the header link, so the next Tab is 'EXPERIENCE'. 390 reduced: menu 'Projects' -> focus returns to the MENU toggle (Nav.tsx:117), and the next Tab goes to 'View projects' at the top of the page. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and makes the nav useless for keyboard users.
file_line: components/Nav.tsx:112-121 (go: preventDefault + scrollToTarget, focus not moved); lib/scroll.ts:31-43
suggested_fix: In scrollToTarget, after resolving the element, move focus to it: give each section (or its h2) tabIndex={-1}, then call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }), from Lenis's onComplete or right away in the native/reduced branch. For the mobile menu, close it, then focus the target instead of the toggle. Keep the focus ring off containers with [tabindex='-1']:focus{outline:none}.

description: Label in Name failure on the language switch. The visible text is 'EN / FR', but aria-label replaces it with 'Voir le site en français' on /en and 'View the site in English' on /fr, confirmed in the ARIA snapshot: link "Voir le site en français" / text: EN / FR. A speech-input user saying 'click FR' or 'click EN' cannot activate it. Fails WCAG 2.5.3 (A).
suggested_fix: Remove aria-label and let the name include the visible text, e.g. EN... keep 'EN / FR' as real text, then append : Voir le site en français. The computed name becomes 'EN / FR : Voir le site en français' and contains the visible label.

description: Language of parts: the switch's name is in the other language (FR text on the en-CA page, EN text on the fr-CA page) with no lang attribute. An aria-label cannot carry a language, so screen readers read 'Voir le site en français' with the English voice and 'View the site in English' with the French voice. hrefLang is present, but it describes the target, not the label. Fails WCAG 3.1.2 (AA).
suggested_fix: Put the foreign-language phrase in real (visually hidden) text wrapped in <span lang={other}> inside the link, rather than in aria-label (combine with the 2.5.3 fix).

description: Opening the mobile menu with the keyboard doesn't move focus into the drawer in full-motion mode. After Enter on MENU, document.activeElement is still the 'CLOSE'/'FERMER' toggle immediately, at +60ms and at +1.2s (390 en, 375 fr). Cause: gsap.fromTo(el,{autoAlpha:0},...) sets visibility:hidden synchronously (Nav.tsx:78), so the el.querySelector('a').focus() two lines later (Nav.tsx:84) targets a link inside a visibility:hidden container and silently fails. With reduced motion (duration 0) focus correctly lands on 'About'. The intended focus management only works for some users.
suggested_fix: Set visibility before focusing: gsap.set(el,{display:'flex',visibility:'visible',opacity:0}); gsap.to(el,{opacity:1,...}); then focus the first link. Or focus inside the tween's onStart, or in requestAnimationFrame after the first render.

description: Escape closes the mobile menu but drops focus to <body>. With focus on a menu link, pressing Escape leaves activeElement=body after 800ms, because the drawer goes display:none and the toggle is not refocused. The next Tab restarts from the top of the document ('View projects'), not from the Menu button. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (A) focus return. Only the link-click path (go) returns focus to the toggle.
suggested_fix: const onKey = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { setOpen(false); toggle.current?.focus(); } }. Do the same whenever the menu closes while focus is inside #mobile-menu (e.g. the resize-to-md close at Nav.tsx:89-90).

description: The focus ring on mobile menu links is clipped. Each <li> is overflow-hidden (it masks the rise-in animation), and it cuts off the 2px copper outline (offset 4px) on the top, left and right. Measured: a=[24,512,366,560], li=[24,512,366,573], outline extent 6px, so top/left/right are clipped and only the bottom edge shows, as a thin copper line that looks like the li's own border-b. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) indicator badly degraded (2.4.13 fails).
suggested_fix:
Move the mask off the focusable element:
  • ...
    • , animating the inner span. Or give .menu-item:focus-visible an inset treatment (outline-offset:-2px, or a copper text/bar colour change).

description: With the menu open, main and footer are now inert, but the skip link is not. Tab past the last item ('Contact') leaves the page and wraps to 'Skip to content', which appears over the drawer. Its target #main is inert, so activating it does nothing while the page stays locked. Tab sequence: About, Projects, Experience, Contact, body, SKIP TO CONTENT, Logo, EN/FR, CLOSE.
suggested_fix: Add document.querySelector('.skip-link') to the `behind` list, or keep focus cycling between the header controls and the menu links while open.

description: The menu toggle changes its accessible name ('Menu' -> 'Close' / 'Fermer') and also flips aria-expanded, so screen readers announce 'Close, button, expanded', a double state signal. The disclosure pattern recommends a stable name plus aria-expanded.
suggested_fix: Keep the visible 'Menu'/'Close' swap but give the button a stable accessible name (aria-label="Menu"), or keep the text swap and drop reliance on aria-expanded wording. Don't do both.

description: The current language is shown by colour alone: active 'EN' is paper and inactive 'FR' is mute, a 2.73:1 difference, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.1 asks for when colour is the only cue. The separator '/' is #2a2d33 on ink at 1.42:1. There is no aria-current or text alternative. The page content makes the language obvious, hence P3.
suggested_fix: Add a non-colour cue to the active code (underline or font-weight) and raise the separator to text-mute. Say which language is current in the sr-only text.

description: Scroll-reveal content is removed from the accessibility tree until it is scrolled into view. Pass-1 CSS had html.js [data-reveal]{visibility:hidden}. At 1440 en motion, at load with scrollY 0, 29 [data-reveal]/[data-intro] elements holding 3,272 of 9,631 characters in <main> are visibility:hidden. The ARIA snapshot shows About paragraphs missing and the experience and skills lists empty. Screen-reader users reading or navigating by element skip this content entirely, and it isn't focusable. Fails WCAG 1.3.2 / 4.1.2 (A). NOTE: the uncommitted working tree (globals.css + Reveals.tsx) switches reveals to opacity:0. Verify after commit, and also make sure an opacity-0 element that receives focus is revealed (focusin -> run its reveal) so keyboard users never focus invisible content.
suggested_fix: Animate opacity/transform only (never visibility or autoAlpha) for [data-reveal]. Add a document-level focusin listener that force-completes the reveal of the focused element's [data-reveal] ancestor.

description: During the ~2.8s boot overlay, keyboard focus goes behind the opaque overlay, and the page is left scrolled mid-way. Tab presses at t=700ms: 'Skip to content', then '01 · Leads', '02 · Designs', '03 · Demo', all covered by div.boot-half--bottom (elementFromPoint). Focusing them scrolls the locked page, and when the boot ends scrollY=8238 (Projects), so the user never sees the hero and starts mid-page. Fails WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA) and 2.4.3.
suggested_fix: While booting, set inert on header, #main and footer (remove it in onComplete). Or skip the intro on the first keydown/pointerdown: window.addEventListener('keydown', () => tl.progress(1), { once: true }). Also re-run window.scrollTo(0,0) in onComplete if focus hasn't moved.

description: The custom cursor hides the OS pointer for everyone with a fine pointer, with no opt-out. html.has-cursor *{cursor:none!important} removes the user's enlarged or high-contrast system pointer and replaces it with a 6px paper dot plus a ring that lags by 0.45s. The dot is 1.19:1 against white surfaces and the ring (paper at 35%) is 2.84:1 on ink. With forced-colors active, the cursor still activates (QUERY ignores forced-colors): the dot keeps background rgb(255,255,255) on the white Canvas, and the ring is forced to black, so it vanishes over black text. The real pointer is effectively lost.
suggested_fix: Extend QUERY with 'and (forced-colors: none) and (prefers-contrast: no-preference)'. Better: don't set cursor:none; draw the ring as an addition to the native pointer, so the OS pointer and its accessibility settings always survive.

description: The header is visibility:hidden for 0.9s+ after load (data-intro, then autoAlpha 0 -> 1 with delay 0.9 and duration 1.4), and until ~2.9s on a first visit. Header links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree during that time. A Tab 150ms after load gives 'Skip to content' -> 'View projects' -> 'Download CV', skipping the whole header, and VoiceOver's auto-read on load starts without the banner.
suggested_fix: Fade the header with opacity only (gsap.fromTo(el,{opacity:0,y:-16},{opacity:1,...})) and exclude header from the visibility:hidden [data-intro] rule, so it stays focusable while it fades in.

description: Decorative loops run forever with no on-page pause: the grain shifts every 0.18s (steps(5) over 0.9s, infinite), plus the status-dot ping (2s infinite) and the hero hint-wire spark (2.2s infinite). They stop only when the OS reduce-motion setting is on or the device has no hover (grain). WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) applies to auto-starting motion that lasts over 5s beside other content. These are decorative, so P3, but a distraction for users with attention or vestibular sensitivities who haven't set the OS flag.
suggested_fix: Stop the loops after a few cycles (animation-iteration-count: 3 for ping and wire), and pause the grain when the page isn't scrolling, or drop the grain animation (a static grain looks nearly identical at 6% opacity).

description: Pass-1 skip link: after Enter on 'Skip to content', document.activeElement is <body> (the #main target had no tabindex). Chrome still moves the sequential start point (the next Tab is 'View projects'), but Safari/VoiceOver and older AT don't reliably follow a non-focusable target. NOTE: the uncommitted page.tsx adds tabIndex={-1} to <main>. Verify it after commit.
suggested_fix: Keep <main id="main" tabIndex={-1}> with #main:focus{outline:none}. Under Lenis, make sure the anchors handler doesn't preventDefault the fragment navigation; if it does, focus #main manually.

description: The 'View projects' CTA scrolls to #projects but doesn't move focus. Reduced 1440: after Enter, scrollY=6640 with focus still on the CTA, and the next Tab lands on 'Download CV' and throws the page back to scrollY 1198 (the hero). Motion 1440: after Enter, the scroll timeline sets .hero-hud-scroll to autoAlpha 0, so the focused CTA becomes visibility:hidden and focus drops to <body> (activeElement=body). Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (A).
suggested_fix: Same fix as the nav: scrollToTarget should focus the target (#projects with tabIndex={-1}, or its h2) with preventScroll once the scroll starts or finishes. Hide the hero HUD with opacity only (not autoAlpha) so it doesn't take the focused element away mid-interaction.

description: Reflow/zoom: on short viewports the hero's text overlaps. 320x256: the 'View projects' button covers 'SUTJIAN' (82x59px overlap), and the header's Logo, EN/FR and MENU sit on top of the eyebrow (overlaps 24x24, 55x12, 34x35). 480x300: both CTAs overlap name line 2 (36x16, 124x16) and the status overlaps it too (116x8). 640x310: 'Download CV' overlaps the name (26x14). Cause: the sticky frame is h-svh overflow-hidden, and the name block is flex-1 min-h-0 while the h1's minimum font is 3.4rem, so the name spills into the bottom row. Fails WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA).
suggested_fix: Under the short variant, let the frame grow (min-h-svh instead of h-svh, and no overflow-hidden in reduced motion), or lower the h1 minimum (e.g. clamp(2.2rem, …) with short:) and add pt equal to the header height (4rem) so the eyebrow always clears the fixed header.

description: The tagline ('I like building things, from AI agents to full websites…') is display:none on every viewport 500px tall or less. That covers landscape phones and desktop users zoomed to 200% on a 1440x900 screen (720x450), who lose the only descriptive sentence in the hero, for sighted and screen-reader users alike (display:none). Content loss on zoom fails WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10 (AA).
suggested_fix: Don't hide it. In the short variant render it at a smaller size or with line-clamp, or move it below the name block and let the hero frame grow (see the reflow fix).

viewport: 375, 1440 (reduced motion; also motion before the intro completes)
description: Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12, AA): with the standard overrides (letter-spacing .12em, word-spacing .16em, line-height 1.5), the name is clipped. At 375, 'Gregory' has scrollWidth 382 vs clientWidth 327 and renders 'GREGOR', and 'Sutjian' 348 vs 327 renders 'SUTJIA'. At 1440, 'Gregory' is 1337 vs 1328. Cause: .hero-name-line keeps overflow-hidden permanently in reduced motion (it is only released in the intro's onComplete), combined with a viewport-width font size.
suggested_fix: Apply the mask only when the intro will play: add overflow-hidden from JS in the motion branch, or use a class like motion-safe:overflow-hidden. Or clip vertically only (overflow-x: visible; overflow-y: clip), which still masks the rising letters.

description: 'Download CV' starts a file download (download attribute, 79 KB PDF) with no file type or size in its name. Users of AT, and users on metered data, aren't told it's a PDF download rather than a page. WCAG 2.4.4 best practice.
suggested_fix: Append visually hidden or visible text: 'Download CV (PDF, 79 KB)', localized ('(PDF, 79 Ko)').

description: Once the hero has scrolled about 15% of its length, the timeline sets the CTAs and eyebrow to visibility:hidden (autoAlpha 0), so they drop out of the tab order. Shift+Tab from the first Projects tab jumps straight to EN/FR in the header ('01 · LEADS' -> 'EN / FR'), and the hero's CV download can only be reached at scroll top. In reduced motion the sequence includes them ('01 · LEADS' -> 'DOWNLOAD CV' -> 'VIEW PROJECTS').
suggested_fix: Tween opacity instead of autoAlpha for .hero-hud-scroll/.hero-eyebrow, and on focusin inside #top scroll the hero back to its start (scrollToTarget(0)) so a focused CTA is always visible.

description: Reduced-motion users get a 'dead scroll'. The hero section stays h-[170vh] / md:h-[190vh] with a sticky frame that nothing animates, so for 70-90vh of scrolling nothing on screen moves, which looks like a frozen page or a broken wheel. This is the static version, yet it keeps the height the scroll animation needed.
suggested_fix: Under prefers-reduced-motion use motion-reduce:h-auto on the section and a non-sticky min-h-svh frame.

description:
In full-motion mode, screen readers get nothing from the statement. SplitText's default aria:'auto' puts aria-hidden on all 31 (EN) / 41 (FR) word elements and moves the text into aria-label on the

, and aria-label is prohibited on role=paragraph (axe aria-prohibited-attr, serious; axe was only run in reduced mode in the pass-1 audit, so this was missed). The Chrome AX tree has 0 non-ignored text nodes for the sentence, and the ARIA snapshot shows 'paragraph: - emphasis' with no text. NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver generally ignore aria-label on

, so the page's key sentence is silent. The emphasis is lost too. Reduced motion is unaffected. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 / 4.1.2 (A).
suggested_fix:
Pass aria:'hidden' and add a screen-reader copy:

next to an aria-hidden visual

. Alternatively pass aria:'none' so the word spans stay readable (some screen readers then pause per word, so the sr-only copy is preferred). Add axe runs in motion mode to the audit.

description: Unlit words sit at opacity 0.13, which is 1.34:1 against ink (paper #edebe6 at 13% over #0b0c0e). The large-text minimum of 3:1 needs opacity 0.37 or more (0.40 gives 3.37:1). The words light in reading order across the scrub (start 'top 45%', end 'bottom 105%'), so most of the 120vh pin shows the tail of the sentence below 3:1. The full sentence is readable at once only in the last ~5vh of the pin, and scrolling back up dims text the user has already read. Fails WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) for the dimmed state.
suggested_fix: Raise the floor to opacity 0.4 (3.37:1) and end the scrub earlier (e.g. end: 'bottom 150%') so the sentence stays fully lit for a real dwell before the pin releases.

description: The region label is duplicated and hard-coded. The <section> has aria-label 'In one sentence' / 'En une phrase', and the first child is a visible paragraph with the same text, so screen readers announce 'In one sentence, region' followed by 'In one sentence'. The strings also live in the component instead of content/site.ts (they will drift from translations).
suggested_fix:
Give the label

an id and use aria-labelledby on the section (or drop the region naming), and move both strings to content/site.ts.

description: At 400% zoom the pinned sentence doesn't fit its frame. The sticky frame is h-svh (256px) with justify-center, and the content is 337px tall, so about 40px overflows above and below. While pinned, the first line ('My favourite part') and the label sit above the viewport and can't be scrolled into view. The screenshot starts at 'of building'. The text can only be read in pieces while it enters and leaves. WCAG 1.4.10.
suggested_fix: Use justify-content: safe center (Tailwind justify-center-safe) plus min-h-svh instead of h-svh, or drop the sticky pin under short heights / reduced motion.

description: In reduced motion the section keeps h-[220vh] with a static sticky frame, so about 120vh of scrolling moves nothing. Together with the hero's 70-90vh, reduced-motion users scroll roughly two screens with no visible change.
suggested_fix: motion-reduce:h-auto on the section and motion-reduce:static / min-h-[60svh] on the frame.
